newsitem.title: USA: US Commerce official urges test of low joblessness.
newsitem.headline: US Commerce official urges test of low joblessness.

text.p: A U.S. Commerce Department official on Tuesday urged a test of the lower limits of non-inflationary U.S. unemployment.

"What I think we can do is test the lower levels of unemployment," said Paul London, deputy undersecretary for Commerce told a luncheon of the National Economists Club. "I don't think it's a risky thing to do when you have this much competition in the economy."
London said the high level of competition would make a rise in inflation unlikely.
The U.S. unemployment rate is currently at 5.1 percent -- a level that some economists fear is low enough to produce enough wage pressures to push inflation higher.

Last week, Joseph Stiglitz, chairman of the White House Council of Economic Advisers, and U.S. Labor Secretary Robert Reich both played down the potential for a rise in inflation stemming from the low unemployment rate.
